main_result: For a finite-dimensional complex vector space V, integers a>=2 and b>=a(a-1), the canonical Foulkes-Howe map mu: Sym^b(Sym^a V) -> Sym^a(Sym^b V), sending a product of b a-th powers u_1^a...u_b^a to (u_1...u_b)^a, is surjective. Equivalently A_b = R_b in the invariant-tensor model. The bound does not depend on dim V. A corollary says a GL(V)-equivariant embedding Sym^a(Sym^b V) -> Sym^b(Sym^a V) exists in the same range. I checked the argument line by line and found no fatal gap.
proof_strategy: Lemma (criterion) dualizes surjectivity of mu into the statement that a symmetric a-linear form T on Sym^b V vanishing on the diagonal of all products of b vectors must be zero. This uses the averaging isomorphism and the invariant-tensor model R_b. Proposition (vanishing) is proved by induction on a. Step 1 factors x^r + c t^r over C to get T(x^rQ,...,x^rQ,t^rQ)=0 from the diagonal hypothesis. Step 2 applies derivative operators D_{y_k}{t} and uses the injectivity lemma (Fischer inner product and norm identity N_U - N_Y) to replace t^rQ by t^b. Step 3 applies the induction hypothesis to an r-linear form on Sym^m V. Step 4 applies r^2 operators D_x{v_i} to remove the common factor x^r, with the degree inequality m >= r^2 ensuring injectivity at each step. Step 5 uses the spanning of pure powers. I could follow every degree count and the derivative rule.
hardest_part: Step 4 of Proposition (vanishing): the degree bookkeeping for f_{i,s} (which blocks contribute x^r, the factorial coefficients) and the passage from polynomial identities in vector variables to evaluated identities via the zero principle. I rechecked the counts (p-q >= 2 using m >= r^2) and they agree, but this is the place where a sign, index or off-by-one slip would be easiest to miss. I did not independently recheck the cited literature claims.

main_result: For a finite-dimensional complex vector space V, a >= 2 and b >= a(a-1), the canonical Foulkes-Howe map Sym^b(Sym^a V) -> Sym^a(Sym^b V) is surjective. Equivalently, the subalgebra generated by R_1 in the invariant algebra R = ((Sym V)^{\otimes a})^{S_a} fills R_b. The corollary is a GL(V)-equivariant embedding Sym^a(Sym^b V) into Sym^b(Sym^a V) for b >= a(a-1), obtained by complete reducibility. The bound does not depend on dim V.
proof_strategy: Averaging identifies R_b with Sym^a(Sym^b V), and a duality argument (Lemma criterion) reduces surjectivity to: a symmetric a-linear form on Sym^b V that vanishes on the diagonal of products of b vectors is zero. Proposition (vanishing) proves this by induction on a with r = a-1 and m = b-r. Step 1 uses splitting of X^r + cY^r over C and the linear-in-c coefficient to get T(x^rQ,...,x^rQ,t^rQ)=0. Step 2 frees the last slot by applying derivatives D_{y_k,t} and cancels them with Corollary (peel), using injectivity of D_{Y,U} on bihomogeneous polynomials with p>q (Lemma shift, proved via the Fischer adjoint and the commutator N_U - N_Y). Step 3 applies the induction hypothesis to the r-linear form (Q_1..Q_r) -> T(x^rQ_1,...,x^rQ_r,t^b). Step 4 applies D_{x,v_i} r times per slot to remove the common factor x^r and concludes by spanning with pure powers. I checked the Fischer adjoint identity, the commutator sign, the polarization identity, the derivative rule, the G_k normalisations, and the degree counts in Steps 2 and 4; all check out on my reading. The induction formula (4a) was accepted by me only after reconstructing it myself.
hardest_part: The hardest part to verify was Step 4: the explicit closed formula (4a) for f_{i,s} with its factorial prefactors (b!/m!)^{i-1} b!/(b-s)!, which is asserted to follow by induction on (i,s) without writing the induction, and the degree bookkeeping p = b-s, q = (i-1)r+s that feeds Corollary (peel). I reconstructed both and they agree with the text, but I had to do the work myself. The Fischer-adjoint and commutator computation in Lemma shift is also easy to get wrong in sign and conjugation, and I only verified it by direct monomial computation.

main_result: For a>=2, b>=a(a-1) and any finite-dimensional complex V, the canonical map mu: Sym^b(Sym^a V) -> Sym^a(Sym^b V) (sending a product of b a-th powers u_1^a...u_b^a to (u_1...u_b)^a) is surjective. Equivalently, the image A_b of the product map in the invariant-tensor algebra R equals R_b. Corollary: a GL(V)-equivariant embedding Sym^a(Sym^b V) -> Sym^b(Sym^a V) exists in the same range (e.g. a=6, b>=30), by complete reducibility.
proof_strategy: Surjectivity is reduced (Lemma criterion, via averaging and polarization) to: a symmetric a-linear form T on Sym^b V vanishing on all b-th-power-of-product diagonals is zero. Proposition (induction on a) shows T(v_1^b,...,v_r^b,t^b)=0 with r=a-1, m=b-r>=r^2. Step 1 uses that X^r+cY^r splits over C to get T(x^rQ,...,x^rQ,t^rQ)=0; Step 2 uses a chain of m derivative operators D_{y_k,t} (injective by a norm/commutator argument, Lemma shift) to free the last slot; Step 3 applies induction to the r-linear form on Sym^m V; Step 4 applies r^2 operators D_{x,v_i} to free the common x^r factor, again using injectivity. I checked the degree bookkeeping in Steps 2 and 4, the commutator identity D'D-DD'=N_U-N_Y, the norm identity, the polarization identity, and the a=2 sanity check; these are consistent. Literature statements (Brion, Raicu-Sam-Weyman, Landsberg Problem 7.19, CIM kernel claims) are unverifiable from the text and were not checked.
hardest_part: The nested derivative bookkeeping in Step 4 (formula (4a) for f_{i,s} with the constants (b!/m!)^{i-1} b!/(b-s)!, and the x-degree (i-1)r+s versus v_i-degree b-s), together with the claim that each Corollary hypothesis p_j>q_j holds at every stage. I checked it by hand and it is consistent, but it is long and I would not trust a quick read to catch an off-by-one. The literature identifications (Problem 7.19 notation, CIM kernel at (5,5),(6,6)) I could not verify at all.
